title: Finiteness: the global sections are perfect at the point
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, an integer $r\geq1$, put $q=p^r$, let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and fix an algebraic closure $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth of relative dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, separated of finite type and geometrically connected, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $a_X:X\to s$ be the structure morphism, as in [sk-def-set]. For each coefficient stage $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, with the finite-Tor and coefficient-stage conventions of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use the ordinary coefficient complexes $C=R\Gamma(X,K)$ and $C_c=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], and write $B^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(B,\Lambda)$ for a point complex $B$.

Then $C,C_c,C^\vee,C_c^\vee$ are perfect point complexes in the sense of [sk-def-perfect]. At finite level they are bounded with finite cohomology and finite Tor amplitude. At $\mathcal O_E$ they have bounded finitely generated cohomology and are perfect, and their finite reductions are perfect with one common Tor amplitude independent of $n$. At the field stages $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ they are bounded with finite-dimensional cohomology.

proof.text: The hypotheses on $X_0$ and the coefficients are exactly those of [sk-def-set]. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $X$ is separated of finite type over the field $k$. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], choose a nonnegative integer $D$ bounding its Krull dimension. We will use [thm-pod-point-perfectness] with this bound $D$, the same $X_0$, and the same $K$. Its opening sentence retains the finite-field datum and coefficient stages of the Poincare conventions but explicitly permits arbitrary separated finite-type $X_0$; it does not assume the exceptional-adjoint admissibility from the conventions. Its hypothesis $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ is the same finite-Tor category [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and its $R\Gamma,R\Gamma_c$ are the same point-fibre constructions [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Thus every hypothesis of that theorem holds, without adding properness, admissibility, or a Weil structure to $K$.

source.place: Proof, Step 1: geometric and coefficient hypotheses; the unit record explicitly names thm:pod-point-perfectness as its point-complex interface

proof.text: At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ apply clause 1 of [thm-pod-point-perfectness]. It states boundedness, finite cohomology and finite Tor amplitude for all four point complexes, and gives bounded finite free representatives. Finite free modules are finite projective (the identity splits the free module from itself), so these representatives give precisely the perfect point complexes of [sk-def-perfect]. In particular this includes the finite compact-support perfectness from which the present lemma starts; ordinary cohomology and both point duals are covered by the same clause.

source.place: Proof, Steps 1 and 2: finite-level bounded finiteness, finite Tor amplitude and perfectness

proof.text: At $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ apply clause 2 of [thm-pod-point-perfectness] to the same integral $K$. It asserts that all four complexes belong to $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$ and are perfect, that reduction of each is the corresponding finite-level complex of $K_n$, and that these reductions have a Tor interval independent of $n$. The perfectness asserted there is quasi-isomorphism to a bounded complex of finite projective $\mathcal O_E$-modules, which is exactly the equivalent form of a perfect point complex in [sk-def-perfect]. These are the integral conclusion and its required common amplitude. The duals here are duals of the point complexes, as in the theorem, so this application does not identify a sheaf coefficient dual with a point dual.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: integral reconstruction and the common finite-reduction amplitude

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$ and $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ apply clause 3 of [thm-pod-point-perfectness]. It states bounded finite-dimensional cohomology for each of $C,C_c,C^\vee,C_c^\vee$ at these very coefficient stages. By the field characterization in [sk-def-perfect], these are perfect point complexes. Together with the finite and integral cases above, this gives the assertion at every stage.
